title: Week 4 Assessment: Working With People
intro: This assessment checks how you behave and decide when working with people: etiquette, presentation, emotions, conflict, networking and stress. Part A is auto-graded from the lessons you completed. Part B has a decision scenario, a role-play and a written task.

items.prompt: You are invited to an on-campus company event the day after an all-night project push. You are tired and your formal clothes are unwashed. What is the best approach?

options.text: Skip the event without telling anyone.
Prepare clean, neat, simple clothes, arrive on time and keep introductions short and polite.
options.feedback: Basic grooming and punctuality create a good impression.

options.text: Wear the same crumpled clothes and avoid eye contact.

options.feedback: This signals low interest in the host.

items.why: Neat basics, punctuality and polite manners matter more than expensive clothing.

items.setup: At a networking event you promised a senior engineer you would send a resume, but you forgot for a week. You now message them to follow up.

turns.they: Hi, I remember we met. Did you send your resume?

options.text: I am sorry for the delay. I missed sending my resume after we met. I have attached it now with two lines on my ABAP training.
options.feedback: A brief apology with immediate repair.
options.reply: Thank you, I will have a look.

options.text: I was busy, and you also did not follow up.
options.feedback: Blaming the other person damages the relationship.

turns.they: Thanks. What kind of role are you looking for?

options.feedback: A vague answer gives them nothing to act on.

options.text: An entry-level SAP ABAP developer role at a services firm. I am building small reports and practising daily.
options.feedback: A specific target with evidence of effort.
Focusing on money alone gives a poor impression.

turns.they: I might know someone. Can you send a short note I can forward?

options.text: I do not have time to write.
options.feedback: Refusing the help they offer loses the chance.

options.text: Certainly. I will send a three-line summary by tomorrow noon.
options.feedback: Clear commitment that makes the favour easy.

items.why: A brief apology, a specific ask and quick follow-through build networking trust.

items.prompt: You have three deadlines this week, you are sleeping badly and a teammate has not replied. Write 100 to 130 words describing how you would prioritise, protect your recovery and handle the unresponsive teammate.

descriptors.3: Clear ordering by deadline and importance.
Clear follow-up with a deadline and escalation path.

items.modelAnswer: I would list the three tasks, rank them by deadline and impact, and start with the earliest important one in a 50-minute focus block each morning. I would stop work at 11 pm, use slow breathing and a shutdown ritual to protect sleep, and schedule a short walk daily. For the teammate, I would send a clear message today asking for their part by tomorrow noon, offering a quick call if they are stuck, and tell my lead by Thursday if there is still no reply, with facts.
items.guidance: Strong answers rank tasks, protect rest with concrete habits and follow up with the teammate politely, with a deadline and an escalation step. Avoid blaming or vague promises.
